theory.intro: **Parallel box plots** are two box plots drawn on the same scaled axis, so two datasets can be compared at a glance.
facts: Both box plots must share the **same scale**, so the two datasets can be compared directly.
A **narrower box** means the middle of the data is tightly clustered, so that dataset is more consistent.
The **median** splits a dataset in half, so about half the results lie above it and half below.
steps: Read the median, minimum and maximum from each box plot.
Compare the medians to see which dataset is generally higher or lower.
Compare the range (maximum $-$ minimum) and the width of each box to judge spread and consistency.

mastery.question_text: A golf club records scores for the same $40$ players on two courses. Both courses share the same maximum score of $90$. Course A has a range of $80$, and Course B has a range of $50$. Without seeing the minimum scores, which course has the lower minimum score, and what is it?
